You are fixing citations in an answer about the Human Protein Atlas. The answer text stays as it is; only the citations named below change. A citation is an exact span of page text: pick a start word and an end word on the page and copy everything between them character for character, the page's own spelling, capitalization, punctuation and mistakes included. Do not fix, shorten, join, reorder or translate anything; no ellipsis; one continuous passage of 15 to 600 characters. Shorter is safer: the one sentence or clause that carries the fact. A sentence that sums up a list or a table cites several short spans, given as a list: "quote": ["<span>", "<span>"], each one exact. Copy from the page text shown to you, not from memory.
Reply with JSON only: {"citations": [{"n": <number>, "page": <page number>, "quote": "<exact span>" or ["<span>", "<span>"]}], "drop": [<numbers of citations that cannot be copied from the text shown>]}.

Question: What is the current release of the Human Protein Atlas, what new data did it add, and how many antibodies and human genes does the atlas cover in this release?
The answer, which stays as it is:
The current release of the Human Protein Atlas is version 25.1. This release adds Deep Visual Proteomics (DVP) data to the Single Cell resource, providing cell-type resolved MS-based protein profiles across 27 cell types (grouped into 24 classifications) and integrating quantitative proteomics profiles for 20 bulk tissue types, which together give protein profiles for over 12,700 genes [1]. The atlas now contains over 27,800 antibodies that target proteins from more than 17,400 human genes, covering about 88 % of the protein-coding genome [2].

These citations did not check out:
[1] on page 1, too long (651 characters, the limit is 600): "The latest addition to the Single Cell resource is Deep Visual Proteomics (DVP) data. Cell-type resolved MS-based protein profiles across 27 different cell types, representing 14 different tissues, are integrated into the Single Cell resource. A total of 27 cell type shapes (with 3-5 replicates each), grouped into 24 cell types used for classifications, are included in this release. Tissue Quantitative proteomics profiles (MS-based) for bulk tissue samples are integrated to the Tissue resource. 20 different tissue types, overlapping with the DVP samples are integrated to the gene-summary pages, providing protein profiles for over 12,700 genes."
Give the shortest span that carries the fact, or several short spans as a list in quote.

The text you may copy from:
--- Page 1, section 0: Protein Atlas version 25.1
Single Cell The latest addition to the Single Cell resource is Deep Visual Proteomics (DVP) data. Cell-type resolved MS-based protein profiles across 27 different cell types, representing 14 different tissues, are integrated into the Single Cell resource. Selected Single Cell Type data are matched to the DVP samples to facilitate a side-by-side comparison of RNA and protein data, accompanied by specificity overlap and agreement scores for systematic RNA-to-protein comparisons. A total of 27 cell type shapes (with 3-5 replicates each), grouped into 24 cell types used for classifications, are included in this release. Tissue Quantitative proteomics profiles (MS-based) for bulk tissue samples are integrated to the Tissue resource. 20 different tissue types, overlapping with the DVP samples are integrated to the gene-summary pages, providing protein profiles for over 12,700 genes.

--- Page 1, section 1: Protein Atlas version 25.0
Twenty-fifth major release of the Human Protein Atlas with over 27,800 antibodies, targeting proteins from over 17,400 human genes (~88% of the human protein-coding genes). 9 separate resources with data covering various aspects of human protein-coding genes. Tissue & Cancer In total 3,937 proteins are validated with Enhanced validation strategies. 14 new antibodies were added. The standard IHC profiling of one antibody was updated and all tissue & cancer images were replaced with new data resulting from restaining of the antibody. Tissue The Tissue resource has expanded the extended protein profiling with eight new tissue samples, including e.g. choroid plexus, efferent ducts, ovary and different phases of placental development. Additional 277 proteins were validated with IHC on extended tissue samples. In total, 873 proteins have been validated on 29 different extended tissue samples. Multiplex tissue profiling has been updated with a new pancreas antibody panel used to study 77 proteins. Additional 22 proteins were studied in ciliated cells. In total, 1106 proteins have been analyzed using 8 antibody panels. New GTEx RNA-seq samples from blood vessels have been added to the consensus bulk RNA data. Brain Spatial transcriptomics data is now updated. Now 3 cerebellum section and 3 cerebral cortex samples (stereo-seq platform) are added. For each sample a crop including all tissue layers is included and the transcript counts for the main cell types (neurons/Purkinje cells, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, microglia and vascular cells) are calculated for each layer for each sample. Single Cell The updated single cell type data represents 34 different tissue types, from 35 separate data sources. Brain cells are now represented by a subsampling of the brain single nuclei data (Siletti. K, et al.), separated into neuronal and non-neuronal (two cell UMAPs from the same data source). Eye is represented by a dataset of general eye-related cells, as well as a retina sample with only retinal cells (one tissue type but two separate sources and UMAPs). Other changes include: Adrenal gland, pituitary gland (single nuclei), epididymis and urinary bladder are newly added tissues, bronchus is removed, the data source is changed for PMBC/blood, bone marrow, esophagus, lymph node, pancreas, spleen, stomach. Single nuclei data is added to replace previous single cell data for adipose tissue, heart muscle, skeletal muscle and kidney. The updated data includes 154 different cell types representing the whole body, these are grouped into 53 main cell type groups for a better overview and categorization. Cell type specificity is calculated for both 154 cell types and the 53 cell type groups. The 15 color-coded cell icons, previously referred to as cell groups, are now called cell class. Tissue and cell types are now sorted based on the organ system on the tissue resource. Color codes are updated for cell types. Subcellular The subcellular resource now covers the subcellular localization of proteins encoded by 13603 genes (77 added and 8 removed), using a total of 15995 antibodies (134 added and 50 removed). A new assay showing the subcellular localization of proteins encoded by 643 genes in human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) has been added. Image embeddings generated using the self-supervised machine learning model SubCell (1) are now availiable under Downloadable data. 1) SubCell: Vision foundation models for microscopy capture single-cell biology Ankit Gupta, Zoe Wefers, Konstantin Kahnert, Jan N. Hansen, Will Leineweber, Anthony Cesnik, Dan Lu, Ulrika Axelsson, Frederic Ballllosera Navarro, Theofanis Karaletsos, Emma Lundberg bioRxiv 2024.12.06.627299; doi: https://doi.org/10.1101/2024.12.06.627299 Blood The blood resource has been expanded with over 2,500 samples profiled using two complementary plasma proteomics technologies: the Olink Explore HT and the SomaScan 11K platforms, measuring over 5,400 and 9,500 proteins, respectively. The samples represent 30 cohorts, including healthy individuals as well as patients with cardiovascular, metabolic, cancer, psychiatric, neurologic, autoimmune, and infectious diseases. This cross-platform, pan-disease dataset complements the previously released data generated with the Olink Explore 1536 platform, enabling exploration of pan-disease profiles for thousands of proteins and investigation of how protein levels relate to age, sex, and BMI across platforms. Additionally, the Olink HT longitudinal dataset, following children from early life into adulthood, has been complemented with SomaScan data. Complementing these datasets, we applied targeted proteomics with qRePS internal standards to the pregnancy cohort also quantified by Olink HT and SomaScan 11k, absolutely quantifying >100 plasma proteins in molar units (pmol/µl). Structure The Structure resource presents the in-house generated AlphaFold 2 predicted three-dimensional structures of 83795 protein isoforms for 19904 human genes with options to display different protein features as well as missense data from Ensembl Variant and AlphaMissense. Interaction The Interaction resource has expanded and now includes in-house generated AlphaFold 3 predicted three-dimensional structures for 22979 Consensus network interactions for 7855 genes in addition to interaction networks integrated with protein expression, location and classification data for 15216 genes. CAB015397 (DNA meiotic recombinase 1) stained images have been omitted and replaced with images from a more recent staining with the same antibody. HPA002697 has been omitted due to antibody staining not supported by experimental data. An alternative antibody HPA002696 has been added. HPA003359 has been omitted due to qualitative reasons. An alternative antibody CAB080429 has been added. CAB015464 has been omitted due to qualitative reasons. An alternative antibody HPA051160 has been added.
